## Problem 1: Assignment in `R`

Consider the following `R` code. 


::: {.cell}

```{.r .cell-code}
x <- 2
y <- x * 3
z <- x + y
```
:::


What are the values of `x`, `y`, and `z`? In other words, what would the following code return? 


::: {.cell}

```{.r .cell-code}
print(x)
print(y)
print(z)
```
:::



\vspace{5em}


## Problem 2: Algebra

Expand (parts a., b.) or simplify (parts c., d.) the following expressions:

a. $\displaystyle\sum_{i=2}^4 X_{i-1}\times X_i$
\vspace{5em}

b. $\displaystyle\prod_{i=1}^4 (X_i)^{i^2-1}$
\vspace{5em}

c. $\displaystyle e^{a+\log(b)}$
\vspace{5em}

d. $\displaystyle e^{a}\times e^{b} \times e^{0}$

\newpage



## Problem 3: Loss Functions


a. Let $n$ be the sample size, $y_i$ be the *observed* response variable values for the $i$th observation, and $\hat y_i$ be the *predicted* response variable value for the $i$th observation. Write down the mean zero-one loss, mean absolute deviation, and mean squared error using these terms (and any other algebraic symbols you may need).


\vspace{20em}


b. Calculate the mean zero-one loss, the mean absolute deviation, and the mean squared error for the dataset of observed values and predictions shown below. 


::: {.cell}
::: {.cell-output-display}


| observed| predicted|
|--------:|---------:|
|      3.5|       1.5|
|      1.0|       1.0|
|      0.0|      -2.0|
|      5.0|       2.0|


:::
:::



\newpage



c. On the following scatterplot, do your best to draw the following three lines: one that minimizes the mean zero-one loss, one that minimizes the mean absolute deviation, and one that minimizes the mean squared error. Please use three different colors to draw these lines, and indicate which color corresponds to which loss function.



::: {.cell layout-align="center"}
::: {.cell-output-display}
![](quiz01_files/figure-pdf/unnamed-chunk-4-1.pdf){fig-align='center'}
:::
:::


\vspace{3em}


d. Recall the definition of bias: 
$$
\mbox{Bias}(\hat y) = \frac{1}{n}\sum_{i=1}^n \hat y_i - y_i.
$$
Which of the lines you drew in part c. (if drawn correctly) will produce the minimal bias for the data points shown in the scatterplot? Which, if any, of these lines will produce unbiased predictions (e.g., $\mbox{Bias}(\hat y) = 0$) for the data points shown in the scatterplot? 


\newpage


::: {.cell}

```{.r .cell-code}
library(MASS)
ggplot(data.frame(x = x, y = y), aes(x = x, y = y)) + 
  geom_point(alpha = 0.4) + 
  geom_smooth(method = "lm", se = F) + 
  geom_smooth(method = "rlm", se = F, color = "seagreen3") + 
  geom_vline(xintercept = 1, color = "tomato", size = 1) + 
  theme_bw() 
```
